title: Why students with disabilities face a digital and remedial learning gap
blurb: The article looks at the digital and remedial learning needs of students with disabilities as education moves towards inclusion. It notes that implementation remains uneven and highlights awareness, teacher training and institutional support as areas for continued work.

title: Teaching students to think in the age of ChatGPT
blurb: The article discusses how education may need to adapt its approach as AI changes the way students write, research and create. It considers the case for teaching students to think critically alongside these tools, a question of growing relevance for school classrooms and teachers.

title: School urges social media curbs for children, SC seeks response from govt, child rights panel
blurb: A plea filed by a school in Indore has asked for limits on children's use of social media, citing growing preoccupation with appearance and followers. The Supreme Court has sought responses from the government and the child rights commission. The matter touches on student wellbeing and how schools and policymakers approach children's online lives.

title: Stronger Law, Safer Exams: India Tightens the Noose on Paper Leaks
blurb: A Press Information Bureau feature describes the legal framework strengthened to safeguard public examinations against paper leaks. It outlines the Union government's measures to keep examinations fair and secure for candidates.

title: Govt ropes in aided, private teachers, PSU staff for Census work
blurb: The Union home ministry has widened the pool of people eligible to work as Census enumerators. Teachers from aided and unaided private schools, as well as staff of public sector undertakings and banks, can now be assigned alongside government school teachers. The change is relevant to how teachers' time is planned alongside school duties.

title: A snapshot of America’s schools: Trends and global comparisons
blurb: A Brookings analysis presents data on trends in American schools and how they compare with schools in other countries, offering a benchmark for where the US stands globally.

title: Gender Inclusion Fund Under NEP 2020: Bridging Gender Gaps In Education
source: IMPRI Impact and Policy Research Institute
blurb: This IMPRI piece looks at the Gender Inclusion Fund under the National Education Policy 2020. It notes that gender disparity in education has historical socio-cultural roots, and presents public policies as efforts to extend equal opportunities to all, including girls and women, in school education.

title: The curriculum of control: How CBSE teaches children to conform, not question
blurb: The opinion piece discusses the role of CBSE schooling in shaping how children learn and engage with questions. The author offers a perspective on pedagogy and classroom culture, which readers may find useful for the wider conversation on curriculum.

title: Ministry of Women and Child Development launches Rashtriya Poshan Maah 2026: Nationwide campaign focuses on dietary diversity, adequate protein intake and fresh hot cooked meals
blurb: The Ministry of Women and Child Development has launched the 9th Rashtriya Poshan Maah 2026, a nationwide nutrition campaign. It focuses on dietary diversity, adequate protein intake and fresh hot cooked meals, which support the health and learning readiness of young children.

title: Centre asks nodal officers to ensure timely verification of NMMSS scholarship applications
blurb: The Department of School Education and Literacy has asked nodal officers at different levels to ensure accurate and timely verification of applications under the National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship Scheme. This followed a regional orientation-cum-review workshop on the scheme held in Bhopal.

title: CIC asks CBSE to conduct surprise checks over alleged dummy school admissions
blurb: The Central Information Commission has recommended that CBSE conduct surprise inspections of affiliated schools to identify alleged dummy admissions and verify compliance with mandatory attendance. The recommendation arose from a complaint concerning private schools in Bhopal and is intended to help establish checks and balances on affiliation conditions.

title: Private school teachers can be deployed for Census work: RGI
blurb: The Centre has amended the Census Rules, 1990, so that states and Union territories can appoint teachers of aided or unaided private bodies as enumerators during the ongoing census. The notification from the Registrar General of India widens the pool of staff who may be deployed for census duties.

title: Govt issues notification on PM CARES scholarship, spells out rules for children without Aadhaar
blurb: The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment notified Aadhaar verification rules for the PM CARES for Children scholarship, covering Classes 1 to 12. Children cannot be denied benefits solely because authentication fails or they lack Aadhaar, subject to alternative verification procedures.

title: Centre expands Census enumerator pool to include private school teachers, clerks
blurb: The Centre has widened the pool of people who can serve as Census enumerators to include private school teachers and clerks.

title: Australian primary students taught basic maths two years later than overseas peers, study reveals
blurb: A study reports that Australian primary students are taught basic maths two years later than peers in other countries. The comparison offers cross-country evidence on when foundational numeracy is introduced in primary school.

title: How Karishma from India broadens access to sexuality education via AI and digital channels
blurb: UNESCO highlights how an initiative called Karishma from India is using AI and digital channels to widen access to sexuality education.

title: Education in Indian Languages: Expanding Economic Opportunity
blurb: This article from The Borgen Project looks at education in Indian languages and its link to economic opportunity. The item came without a summary, so the discussion is only indicated by its title. It appears to explore how learning in familiar languages may widen access to opportunity.

title: CIC flags alleged dummy admissions, recommends surprise checks at CBSE-affiliated schools
blurb: The Central Information Commission has recommended surprise inspections of CBSE-affiliated schools to check alleged dummy admissions and ensure compliance with mandatory attendance rules. The recommendation is aimed at strengthening checks and balances in school affiliation compliance.

title: FutureReady Schools: What Does ‘Being Prepared for Tomorrow’ Really Mean?
blurb: This ORF commentary asks what it means for a school to be future-ready, going beyond smart classrooms, digital platforms and coding offerings. It examines whether readiness lies mainly in technology and infrastructure or in the capabilities built among students, teachers and school leaders, particularly with the rise of generative AI.

title: Closing India’s foundational literacy gap | Hindustan Times
blurb: The Hindustan Times article discusses India's foundational literacy gap and what is needed to close it. It adds to ongoing national conversation on building strong early reading skills, a priority within the foundational learning agenda.

title: Nearly half of all students enrolled in IIT Madras’ school outreach initiative are girls
blurb: Nearly half of the students enrolled in IIT Madras's School Connect outreach initiative are girls. The institute aims to expand the initiative to 25,000 schools across the country in the coming years, building on its existing network of 6,406 partner schools.

title: Centre pushes open schooling via NIOS to achieve 100% enrolment by 2030
blurb: The Centre is promoting open schooling through the National Institute of Open Schooling (NIOS) as one route towards the goal of 100% enrolment by 2030. The step aims to widen flexible pathways for learners to continue their school education.

title: UDISE+ report shows rise in teachers, fall in school dropout rates
blurb: The Ministry of Education released the UDISE+ 2025-26 report, which records teacher numbers rising to 1,02,73,020 from 94,83,294 in 2022-23. Pupil-teacher ratios are reported at 10 at the foundational level and 21 at the secondary level, within the NEP-recommended 30:1. Dropout rates also declined, including at the preparatory level (2.3 to 1.8 per cent) and secondary level (8.2 to 7 per cent).

title: Learning at the Speed of AI: Using Platform Trials to Test AI Innovation
blurb: This Center for Global Development publication looks at how platform trials could be used to test AI innovations more quickly and rigorously. It is relevant for education stakeholders interested in evidence-based approaches to new technology. Further details were not available in the item summary.

title: From assessment to the classroom: using data to improve learning in the Dominican Republic
blurb: UNESCO describes how assessment data is being used to improve learning in the Dominican Republic. The item gave no further detail, but its title points to links between assessment results and classroom practice, an approach relevant to learning-outcome improvement elsewhere.

title: RIE Bhubaneswar Hosts Capacity Building Programme on NEP 2020 & NCF-SE 2023
blurb: NCERT's Department of Curriculum Studies and Development, with RIE Bhubaneswar, concluded a three-day capacity building programme on NEP 2020 and the National Curriculum Framework for School Education 2023. It brought together 51 nodal principals and school leaders from across eastern India. The programme supports school-level implementation of NEP and NCF-SE.

title: Google extends AI teacher training to Bihar, Madhya Pradesh and Sikkim
blurb: Google is expanding its AI training programme for educators through new partnerships with the governments of Bihar, Madhya Pradesh and Sikkim and the Union Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship. More than 80,000 educators have completed the free, self-paced training since May 2026, which covers AI tools for lesson planning and learning materials.

title: DigiLocker, ePathshala to UMANG: Top 5 Must-Have Government Apps For Students in India
blurb: The article lists five government apps useful to students in India, including DigiLocker, ePathshala and UMANG. It describes how these free apps help students reach learning materials, manage important documents and use government services without visiting several offices or websites.

title: Reading and Writing: The Lifeline of Education and Communication
blurb: This op-ed argues that reading and writing should remain central to schooling alongside the growing use of digital tools and AI. The author suggests schools organise reading and writing competitions to strengthen comprehension and writing skills. The piece links these foundational skills to the goals of the National Education Policy.

title: Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan, Objectives, Components, Challenges
blurb: This explainer describes Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan as the Government of India's flagship integrated school-education scheme, covering the continuum from pre-school to Class XII. It outlines the scheme's objectives, components and challenges, and serves as a useful reference on how school education programmes are structured.

title: Three-Day Capacity Building Programme for Nodal School Principals and School Leaders on NEP 2020 and NCF-SE 2023 Concludes at RIE Bhubaneswar
blurb: A three-day capacity building programme for nodal school principals and school leaders on NEP 2020 and NCF-SE 2023 has concluded at RIE Bhubaneswar. The programme supports school leadership in taking forward the national policy and curriculum framework.

title: Ministry of Education organises Orientation-cum-Review Workshop on National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship Scheme (NMMSS) to Strengthen Scholarship Implementation and Verification Processes
blurb: The Ministry of Education held an orientation-cum-review workshop on the National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship Scheme (NMMSS). The workshop focused on strengthening how the scholarship is implemented and how applications are verified.

title: NCERT brings personal finance to Class 9, but can one chapter build money habits?
blurb: NCERT's new Class 9 Social Science textbook includes a chapter, Managing Your Personal Finances, on budgeting, saving, investing, insurance, borrowing and tax. The article discusses how classroom practice and parental involvement will shape lasting money habits.

title: Nilekani suggests AI-made exams: China prints papers in prisons, other countries use question banks to stop leaks | HT Explainers
blurb: An explainer discusses Nandan Nilekani's suggestion of AI-made exams and compares how different countries try to prevent exam paper leaks, including secure printing and question banks.

title: Are Schools Preparing Students for an Outdated World?
blurb: This opinion piece examines whether schools that rely heavily on exams and memorisation prepare students for a world being reshaped by AI. The author discusses why critical thinking, AI literacy and practical problem-solving should be taught alongside core subjects such as mathematics, science, languages and history.

title: Census 2027: P&H High Court Stays Communications Seeking Details Of Private School Teachers For Census...
blurb: The Punjab and Haryana High Court has stayed, for private unaided schools, two communications that sought details of teachers for Census 2027 duty. The interim order followed a petition by a private schools body and applies until the next hearing.

title: Education: A Pathway to Opportunity and Empowerment
blurb: A Press Information Bureau feature titled 'Education: A Pathway to Opportunity and Empowerment' highlights the role of education in expanding opportunities.

title: At World Education Summit 2026, the next test for AI is keeping human connection at the heart of learning
blurb: The 36th Elets World Education Summit 2026 in New Delhi brought together decision-makers from government, schools, higher education and the education-technology ecosystem. Speakers from NITI Aayog, CBSE and other organisations discussed AI, adaptive learning and keeping human connection at the heart of learning.

title: Every School, A Model School
blurb: A PIB feature titled 'Every School, A Model School' presents the Pradhan Mantri Schools for Rising India (PM SHRI) initiative, which was launched on 7 September 2022. The piece positions the scheme as part of the effort to develop model schools, and serves as a handy reference for readers following NEP implementation.

title: Prime Minister highlights the strong contribution of teachers on Teachers' Day
blurb: The Prime Minister highlighted the strong contribution of teachers on Teachers' Day.

title: Bobby Hajjaj for extending primary teacher training duration, PTI capacity boost
blurb: In an interview, Bobby Hajjaj described plans to extend primary teacher training to two-and-a-half to three years and to expand the capacity of Primary Training Institutes six-fold, aiming to raise teaching quality. He also discussed teacher recruitment and promotion, technology in classrooms, the midday meal programme and oversight of private and kindergarten schools.

title: As attacks on schools rise by 33% in 2025, UNESCO calls for stronger protection of education
blurb: UNESCO calls for stronger protection of education as attacks on schools rose by 33 percent in 2025.

title: More children out of school for the 7th year in a row, up to 273 million
blurb: UNESCO reports that the number of children out of school has risen for the seventh year in a row, reaching up to 273 million. No further detail was available in the feed beyond the title.

title: Open minds please: School can't teach children everything but must foster lifelong learning
blurb: This opinion piece argues that schools cannot teach children everything but should foster openness and lifelong learning. Using the example of scientific ideas that changed over time, the author encourages students to ask what else we might be wrong about.

title: By rewriting textbooks, India is weakening spirit of enquiry mandated by the Constitution
blurb: The author discusses changes to school textbooks and their possible bearing on the spirit of enquiry mentioned in the Constitution. The article examines how medieval history is presented to students and reflects on what this means for critical thinking in education.

title: New UNESCO data released on World Teachers’ Day shows the world needs
blurb: UNESCO has released new data on World Teachers' Day, pointing to the global needs of the teaching profession.

title: PM SHRI schools in catch-22 — funds lapse; vendors press for payments
blurb: The Tribune reports that PM SHRI schools face a funding lapse, with vendors pressing for payments. The article draws attention to fund utilisation timelines under the scheme, an area where timely coordination can help schools complete planned work.

title: UNICEF praises India’s progress in girls’ education, says community action is helping curb child...
blurb: UNICEF has praised India's progress in girls' education and noted that community action is helping to curb child-related challenges. The update recognises the national progress made and the role of local communities in keeping girls in school.

title: India's school-to-work push faces test of skills, jobs and apprenticeships
blurb: The government plans to link education and employment databases and expand career counselling in schools. Business Standard reports that experts see apprenticeships, training and job creation as important complements to improve school-to-work outcomes.

title: Under Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0, various steps have been undertaken to improve the infrastructure facilities at Anganwadi Centres
blurb: Under Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0, steps are under way to improve infrastructure at Anganwadi Centres, including construction of 50,000 centres during the 15th Finance Commission cycle in convergence with MGNREGS. More centres are being built under PM JANMAN and Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan, and a Nominee Module in Poshan Tracker supports uninterrupted Take-Home Ration delivery.

title: Teacher recruitment – compounding the challenge
blurb: This article discusses how the introduction of the four-year Integrated Teacher Education Programme by NCTE may affect teacher recruitment and qualification norms across school stages. The author examines implications for teacher availability in India, highlighting an area for careful planning during the transition.

title: CBSE Announces Dates For Class 12 Special Exams In UAE, 6 Other Countries
blurb: CBSE has announced dates for special Class 12 board exams, from October 23 to 28, in seven Middle East countries where papers were disrupted: UAE, Bahrain, Iran, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar and Saudi Arabia. The exams cover 40 subjects, 20 academic and 20 skill, for eligible students assessed under the special scheme introduced on March 27, 2026.

title: Indore school moves Supreme Court seeking curbs on social media use of children | India News
blurb: A school in Indore has filed a public interest litigation in the Supreme Court asking for an enforceable regulatory framework on children's use of social media. The petition argues that protecting minors online is a public responsibility, and the Union government is among the respondents. A hearing date has not yet been set.

title: CBSE Class 12 special exams for West Asian students from October 23 to 28
blurb: CBSE has released a timetable for Class 12 special examinations from October 23 to 28, 2026, for eligible students in seven West Asian countries where regular board papers could not be held earlier. Students may choose the subjects they wish to appear in, and the special exam result will be final and will replace marks awarded under the earlier assessment scheme.

title: UNICEF official praises India's progress on girls' education
blurb: A UNICEF official has praised India's progress on girls' education.

title: Nandan Nilekani pitches for AI generated question papers, nationwide CBT to avoid paper leaks | Education
blurb: Nandan Nilekani suggested generating question papers with AI on the day of the exam, from a large question bank, and moving towards nationwide computer-based testing. His aim is to reduce the risk of paper leaks and lessen any incentive to sell question papers.

title: Gender and education: What is the latest data and evidence?
blurb: UNESCO has published a piece reviewing the latest data and evidence on gender and education. The source gave no further detail, so the specific findings are not described. It is a global reference on progress and gaps in education for girls and boys.

title: New UNESCO data: For every two teachers, the world needs one more
blurb: New UNESCO data indicates that the world needs one additional teacher for every two currently teaching. No further detail was available in the feed beyond the title.

title: SubscriberWrites: From Degrees to Capabilities: Rethinking India’s Education
blurb: In this reader-contributed article, the author discusses how India's education system could place greater emphasis on capabilities rather than degrees. The piece notes that Viksit Bharat will need many more educated Indians and that education can no longer be measured only by years spent in classrooms.

title: DIKSHA: Powering India's Digital Learning Ecosystem
blurb: A Press Information Bureau feature describes DIKSHA as a platform powering India's digital learning ecosystem.

title: Coaching as Compensation: What the Red Fort scheme reveals about school education | Hindustan Times
blurb: This opinion piece considers the proposed nationwide network of free online coaching announced on 15 August 2026. The author notes it can widen access to exam preparation, and argues that stronger school education is key to reducing dependence on coaching, citing a survey figure of 27% of students taking private coaching.

title: Learning for Tomorrow: How El Salvador Is Using AI to Transform Education
blurb: The World Bank describes how El Salvador is modernising education at scale by combining evidence-based teaching practices, data and AI. In sixth-grade classes, digital tools support reading and mathematics lessons aligned with the national curriculum, and teachers can see in real time where students are succeeding or need more support.

title: El Niño Practical Guidance for the Education Sector
blurb: UNICEF has published practical guidance for the education sector on El Niño. Further details were not available in the item summary.

title: Choosing an international curriculum - What are Indian parents really investing in? | Hindustan Times
blurb: The author, an education company founder, examines why Indian parents are choosing international curricula such as IB and Cambridge. The piece notes 274 IB World schools and more than 800 Cambridge schools in India, nearly half of the latter in Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities, and links this to families' aspirations for global exposure.

title: India's primary education crisis: Children are in schools but are they desirably learning ?
blurb: The article discusses a concern raised by Tata Trusts Chairman Noel Tata about the foundations of primary education in India. The author asks whether children acquiring essential competencies in early years is a precondition for excellence in later schooling and skills, and reflects on the gap between enrolment and learning.

title: RTE Students Cannot Demand Automatic Transfer From One Private Unaided School To Another Upon Closure:...
blurb: A court ruling reported by Verdictum states that students admitted under the Right to Education Act cannot demand automatic transfer from one private unaided school to another when the first school closes. The item provides no further detail on the case or the conditions discussed.

title: Only 59 Rural Indian Girls Complete Higher Secondary Education For Every 100 Boys: UNESCO
blurb: A UNESCO report highlights differences in upper-secondary completion across India, with a gender parity index of 0.59 in rural areas compared with 1.00 in urban areas and 0.89 nationally. The findings offer useful evidence on where continued effort can help more rural girls complete higher secondary education.

title: AI in the classroom needs teachers in the driver’s seat, global study finds
blurb: A global study finds that AI in the classroom works best when teachers lead its use. The finding underlines the central role of educators as schools around the world consider how to bring AI into teaching.

title: CBSE’s Digital Evaluation System Overlooks Teachers And Students: Apar Gupta
blurb: Lawyer Apar Gupta discussed CBSE's On-Screen Marking system for Class 10 and 12 answer scripts. He said digitisation should be judged by its benefit to learning and raised points on planning, cybersecurity, accessibility and grievance redressal. The article reports his views without any official response.

title: Principals, Teachers From 24 Schools Discuss Inclusive Education, Teacher Training And Classroom Innovation At
blurb: A two-day Principals and Teachers Conference concluded at the Regional Institute of Education, Bhopal, bringing together educators from 24 schools. Experts discussed inclusive education, 21st-century classroom skills and educational innovations, while participants shared best practices and officials emphasised stronger collaboration between schools and teacher training institutions.

title: Literacy for All
blurb: The Press Information Bureau has published a note titled 'Literacy for All'; the available text does not include its details.

title: NCERT Announces Online Diploma Course In Science Teaching: Registration From October 12
blurb: NCERT has announced an online diploma course in science teaching, with registration starting October 12. The source gave no further detail on eligibility or content. The course is aimed at supporting teachers in building their science teaching skills.

title: Education ministry holds nationwide screening on inclusive education for children with special needs
blurb: The Ministry of Education held a nationwide screening of a 30-minute orientation module on inclusive education for children with special needs, through the PRASHAST portal. The module is available in 12 Indian languages and supports a whole-school approach to inclusion.

title: NCERT releases most revised textbooks up to Class 9
blurb: NCERT has released the most revised textbooks for classes up to Class 9.

title: They still call us ‘jungli’. For Adivasi kids, free school comes at a cost
blurb: The article looks at the experiences of Adivasi children in accessing free schooling and the costs families can still face.

title: From India to France: Why are Gen Z students angry?
blurb: This article compares the School Thik Karo campaign launched in India on August 15 to check basic facilities in government schools with student protests that began in Créteil, France, and spread across Europe. The protests concern crowded classrooms, teacher shortages, school buildings, education costs and school spending. The article discusses common themes in students' concerns.

title: AI-powered scams raise stakes of student data breaches, cybersecurity expert warns
blurb: A cybersecurity expert says EdTech platforms handling student data can face risks through third-party services such as payment gateways and cloud providers. He suggests stronger security checks on each integration to protect children's information.

title: School heads seek law to protect educational institutions, teachers from violence
blurb: School heads are asking for a law to protect educational institutions and teachers from violence. The item reflects a request from school leaders for stronger legal safeguards for the school community.

title: EDUTHON 6.0 BRINGS 1,200+ EDUCATION LEADERS TO CHANDIGARH TO DISCUSS AI AND THE FUTURE OF SCHOOL EDUCATION
blurb: Eduthon 6.0 in Chandigarh brought together more than 1,200 education leaders to discuss artificial intelligence and the future of school education.

title: Union education minister urges students to focus on innovation to build developed India
blurb: Union Minister Prahlad Joshi, speaking in Patna, said education should go beyond rote learning and urged students to focus on innovation for a developed India by 2047. He said NEP 2020 promotes critical thinking and creativity. The Seva Sankalp Abhiyan competitions involved students from 95,195 schools across 38 districts in Bihar.

title: Education Ministry conducts nationwide screening on inclusive education through PRASHAST portal
blurb: The Ministry of Education has conducted a nationwide screening on inclusive education through the PRASHAST portal.
